Ground mismatch: TEN are run-first (38% pass when leading) into a NYG front that bleeds 142 rush yds/game and 0.53 RB1 rushing scores. Tony Pollard is a centerpiece.

The NYG host the TEN as favorites of 3.0, with the total set at 45.5 — a market that implies a NYG 24–21 scoreline. Running the game forward from that baseline, we expect a contest that spends roughly 31% of its snaps with NYG in front, 41% within one score, and 27% with NYG chasing. That distribution is the engine of everything below: game state is what turns a team's tendencies into a specific player's workload, so before we get to individuals it's worth being explicit about how this game is likely to be played.

This is a coin-flip script. With only 3.0 points separating them, neither team projects to spend much time in a blowout state — most of the game lives in the 'close' bucket, where play-calling stays balanced and usage tracks each player's established role rather than being distorted by score. In tight games the stars on both sides see their normal, dependable workloads, and there is less garbage-time leakage to backups.

The Key Matchups

Sneaky value on Darius Slayton (WR2) — TEN leak 44 yds/game to the WR2 role, above the ~36 norm.

Touchdown Board

Tony Pollard is a bell-cow (70% of carries) meeting a defense that allows 0.53 RB rushing TDs/game — strong anytime-TD equity.

Malik Nabers carries TD equity — TEN surrender 0.53 WR1 receiving scores a game.

Game Script, Pace & Environment

A middling 46 total — no strong lean either way; the value is in the individual matchups above, not the game environment.

NYG — a balanced offense

NYG are a balanced offense — their run/pass split by game state tracks the league closely (42% pass when leading vs 44% average), so their players' usage is driven more by role than by any strong situational lean.

Tyrone Tracy Jr. (12 carries, 53 yards) projects to his baseline workload — no strong script push either way in a close game.

Malik Nabers projects for 8 targets and 59 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

Underneath, Theo Johnson (TE, 6 targets, 42 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

TEN — a run-heavy offense

TEN are one of the league's more run-committed offenses: on early downs while leading, they pass just 38% of the time, against a league average of 44% — a genuine clock-bleeding identity, not noise (it holds after shrinking their sample toward the league).

Tony Pollard (14 carries, 62 yards) projects to his baseline workload — no strong script push either way in a close game.

Wan'Dale Robinson projects for 8 targets and 50 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

Underneath, Gunnar Helm (TE, 3 targets, 23 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

What to watch

The single biggest swing factor is availability — use the injury tool in the sidebar to mark anyone out; a starter's absence doesn't just remove his line, it redistributes his targets and carries to specific teammates, and the report and projections rebuild around it. Beyond that: if this game breaks toward the projected 3-point margin, the garbage-time backups (the ◆-flagged rows below) are where soft lines and real edge tend to appear — those depth players get fed in blowouts, and the market is slowest to price them.
